Polishing with nthits and ntedit

Mar Llaberia-Robledillo

2023-05-15

  • Filtering the FASTQ files for polishing
  • Filtering and ordering of contigs

Filtering the FASTQ files for polishing

The first attempts to run ntEdits [@Warren2019] end up with a std::bad_alloc error, which may be due to insufficient memory. The assembly is about 453 million base pairs (<0.5 Gb), which is much less than the 20 Gb-genomes reported to be polished with ntHits in less than 30 minutes with 90 Gb of RAM [@Warren2019] (we have 250 Gb). The main difference between the examples reported in the original article and our attempt may be the size of the bloom filter (BF). While the authors used 17\(\times\) sequence data for the bloom filter, we have probably more than double that (~35\(\times\), in two FASTQ files).

Too much data in the FASTQ files could be the problem. Below, I use vsearch to get statistics of the expected number of errors per read in the first FASTQ file, then I filter the file to reduce the size and remove errors before running the ntcard and nthits programs.

FASTQ1=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_1.fastq.gz
FASTQ2=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_2.fastq.gz

if [ ! -e eestats1.txt ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_eestats2 $FASTQ1 \
           --output eestats1.txt \
           --ee_cutoffs 0.5,0.75,0.85,0.95,1
fi

if [ ! -e eestats2.txt ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_eestats2 $FASTQ2 \
           --output eestats2.txt \
           --ee_cutoffs 0.5,0.75,0.85,0.95,1
fi

if [ ! -e eestats_summary.txt ]; then
   gawk 'BEGIN{
      START = 0
      print "Length\tMaxEE0.50\tMaxEE0.75\tMaxEE0.85\tMaxEE0.95\tMaxEE1.00\tFile"
   }(START == 1){
      gsub(/[\(\)]/, "", $0)
      print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $4 "\t" $6 "\t" $8 "\t" $10 "\tFASTQ1"
   }(/----/){START = 1}' eestats1.txt > eestats_summary.txt
   gawk 'BEGIN{
      START = 0
   }(START == 1){
      gsub(/[\(\)]/, "", $0)
      print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $4 "\t" $6 "\t" $8 "\t" $10 "\tFASTQ2"
   }(/----/){START = 1}' eestats2.txt >> eestats_summary.txt
fi
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
eestats <- read.table('eestats_summary.txt', header = TRUE)
eestats_L <- pivot_longer(eestats, 2:6, names_to = 'MaxEE', values_to = 'NumReads')
ggplot(data = eestats_L, mapping = aes(x = Length, y = NumReads, color = MaxEE)) +
   geom_line() + facet_wrap(~File)

FASTQ1=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_1.fastq.gz
FASTQ2=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_2.fastq.gz

if [ ! -e filtered1.fasta ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_filter $FASTQ1 \
           --fastaout filtered1.fasta \
           --fastq_maxee 0.5
fi

if [ ! -e filtered2.fasta ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_filter $FASTQ2 \
           --fastaout filtered2.fasta \
           --fastq_maxee 0.5
fi
for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e filtered1_k$k.hist ]; then
      ntcard -k $k -t 16 -p filtered1 filtered1.fasta
   fi
done

for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e filtered2_k$k.hist ]; then
      ntcard -k $k -t 16 -p filtered2 filtered2.fasta
   fi
done
k31 <- read.table('filtered1_k31.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k47 <- read.table('filtered1_k47.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k61 <- read.table('filtered1_k61.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
plot(k31$multiplicity, k31$frequency, type = 'l',
     xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(5.0e+05, 1.0e+09),
     log = 'y', xlab = 'Multiplicity',
     ylab = 'Frequency', col = 'darkred')
lines(k47$multiplicity, k47$frequency, col = 'darkgreen')
lines(k61$multiplicity, k61$frequency, col = 'darkblue')
abline(v = 6, col = 'darkred', lty = 2)
#abline(v = 5, col = 'darkgreen', lty = 2)
abline(v = 4, col = 'darkblue', lty = 2)

k31 <- read.table('filtered2_k31.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k47 <- read.table('filtered2_k47.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k61 <- read.table('filtered2_k61.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
plot(k31$multiplicity, k31$frequency, type = 'l',
     xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(5.0e+05, 1.0e+09),
     log = 'y', xlab = 'Multiplicity',
     ylab = 'Frequency', col = 'darkred')
lines(k47$multiplicity, k47$frequency, col = 'darkgreen')
lines(k61$multiplicity, k61$frequency, col = 'darkblue')
abline(v = 6, col = 'darkred', lty = 2)
#abline(v = 5, col = 'darkgreen', lty = 2)
abline(v = 4, col = 'darkblue', lty = 2)

The sequenced reads were shortenned from 150 to 140 bp. The reason why longer kmers have lower coverage peaks is just that any fragment of a chromosome has a lower chance of being fully contained in a fixed-length, randomly located read, the longer the fragment is. The high coverage of error-free 31-mers distinguish them from low-frequency, error-containing 31-mers. Thus, I’d suggest we use \(k=31\) for polishing.

FASTA1=filtered1.fasta
FASTA2=filtered2.fasta

for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e filtered_k$k.bf ]; then
      nthits --threads 16 \
             --kmer $k \
             --pref filtered \
             --outbloom \
             --solid \
             $FASTA1 $FASTA2 1> nthits_k$k.log 2> nthits_k$k.err
   fi
done
ASSEMBLY=../2023-05-12/flye/ONT_PB/assembly.fasta

for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e ntedit_k${k}_edited.fa ]; then
      ntedit -t 32 \
             -f $ASSEMBLY \
             -r filtered_k$k.bf \
             -b ntedit_k$k \
             -v 1 1> ntedit_k$k.log 2> ntedit_k$k.err
   fi
   if [ ! -e changes_k$k.tsv ]; then
   # In the original file, not all lines have the same number of columns.
      cut -f 1,2,3,4,5 ntedit_k${k}_changes.tsv > changes_k$k.tsv
   fi
done
changes_k31 <- read.table('changes_k31.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t',
                          col.names = c('contig', 'position',
                                        'original', 'newbase', 'support'))
changes_k47 <- read.table('changes_k47.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t',
                          col.names = c('contig', 'position',
                                        'original', 'newbase', 'support'))
changes_k61 <- read.table('changes_k61.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t',
                         col.names = c('contig', 'position',
                                       'original', 'newbase', 'support'))
changes_k31$change <- paste(changes_k31$original,
                            changes_k31$newbase,
                            sep = ':')
changes_k47$change <- paste(changes_k47$original,
                            changes_k47$newbase,
                            sep = ':')
changes_k61$change <- paste(changes_k61$original,
                            changes_k61$newbase,
                            sep = ':')

profile31 <- as.data.frame(table(changes_k31$change))
profile31$k <- 31
profile31$RelFreq <- profile31$Freq / sum(profile31$Freq)
profile47 <- as.data.frame(table(changes_k47$change))
profile47$k <- 47
profile47$RelFreq <- profile47$Freq / sum(profile47$Freq)
profile61 <- as.data.frame(table(changes_k61$change))
profile61$k <- 61
profile61$RelFreq <- profile61$Freq / sum(profile61$Freq)
z <- rbind(profile31, profile47, profile61)
z2 <- pivot_wider(z, names_from = k, values_from = c('Freq', 'RelFreq'))
z2[is.na(z2)] <- 0
class(z2) <- 'data.frame'
z2$TotFreq <- z2$Freq_31 + z2$Freq_47 + z2$Freq_61
t <- order(z2$TotFreq, decreasing = TRUE)
class(z) <- 'data.frame'
z$Var1 <- ordered(z$Var1, levels = z2[t, 'Var1'])
z$k <- factor(as.character(z$k))
f <- z$RelFreq >= 0.02
ggplot(z[f,], aes(x = k, y = RelFreq, fill = Var1)) + geom_bar(stat = 'identity')

ggplot(z, aes(x = as.numeric(Var1), y = Freq, color = k)) +
   geom_line() + xlim(0, 20)
## Warning: Removed 4902 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_line()`).

The plots above represent different editions introduced by ntedit with different values of the \(k\). Nothing important. It seems that using \(k=31\) produces more editions, but not qualitatively different from those introduced when using higher values of \(k\).

Filtering and ordering of contigs

For subsequent analyses, it is convenient to have contigs of the assembly ordered by size, decreasingly. I also want to remove contigs of presumed multiplicity larger than 1, according to flye (see 2023-05-13), which are not a large fraction of the assembly.

library(Biostrings)

chosen <- readDNAStringSet('ntedit_k31_edited.fa')
AssInf <- read.table('../2023-05-12/flye/ONT_PB/assembly_info.txt',
                     col.names = c('ctg', 'len', 'cov', 'circ', 'rep',
                                   'mult', 'group', 'path'))
multi1 <- AssInf[AssInf$mult == 1, 'ctg']
multi1 <- intersect(multi1, names(chosen))
chosen <- chosen[multi1]
chosen <- chosen[order(width(chosen), decreasing = TRUE)]
writeXStringSet(chosen, 'assembly.fasta')

I write down in assembly.fasta a filtered and ordered version of the chosen assembly, with a total length of 206254914 nucleotides. Please, use assembly.fasta in this folder as a reference.
